Review complete — verdict: **reject**.

The diff doesn't match the self-report. The worker claimed to resolve the PROGRESS.md conflict by keeping both appended sections in order (HEAD's work-progress-report entry + main's dashboard-hierarchy entry), but the actual diff shows it deleted all three pre-existing accumulated task sections (272 lines: resource-management, project-records/permits/drawings/MoMs, company-dept-dashboard) and replaced them with only a short new entry for this meta-task itself. That contradicts the repo's own append-only PROGRESS.md convention (which the self-report explicitly cites) and destroys documented history — including disclosed open items like the unbuilt WhatsApp integration and an un-pushed cross-repo dependency awaiting sign-off.

No `.github/workflows/**` or schema/auth files are touched, so the hard workflow-scope rule isn't implicated; tier2 here is correctly driven by the heavy-deletion diff shape alone. Given the mismatch between narrative and diff, this needs human reconciliation, not merge. Verdict recorded in `review-verdict.json`.
